name: Kunxian capsule
short: Menstrual disorders, with amenorrhoea in 10 of 20 premenopausal women in one series; authors warn of ovarian failure with Tripterygium preparations. In trials, overall adverse events were not higher.
text: Kunxian capsule is described in the cited abstracts as a newer Tripterygium wilfordii preparation. Its most serious reported harm is reproductive: in a retrospective series of 55 people with IgA nephropathy, 12 of the 20 premenopausal women developed infrequent or irregular periods and ten developed amenorrhoea (absent periods), and the authors said women of childbearing age should be informed of the risk of ovarian failure with Tripterygium preparations. A 2026 meta-analysis of 17 randomized trials (1368 patients) in kidney diseases found menstrual disorders significantly more common with the capsule (5.9% vs 1.8%) and concluded that gonadal inhibition remains an inherent drawback of Tripterygium drugs; the same analysis found fewer adverse reactions overall than in control groups, including liver function impairment (4.0% vs 4.9%), infection (2.4% vs 5.9%) and low white cell counts (1.9% vs 3.8%). In other trials, adverse events did not differ significantly from control in a 48-week randomized trial in 80 people with diabetic kidney disease taking irbesartan, in a prospective cohort of IgA nephropathy comparing the capsule with mycophenolate mofetil (8.9% vs 6.9%), or in a 240-patient randomized open trial in rheumatoid arthritis that included a group taking the capsule with methotrexate. A review noted reports of adverse reactions in multiple body systems. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
